statement:
You are given an array of meeting time intervals `intervals`, where `intervals[i] = [startᵢ, endᵢ]`. Return the **minimum number of conference rooms** needed so that every meeting can be held.

A room freed at time `t` can be reused by a meeting that starts at time `t`.

examples.explanation: `[0,30]` needs its own room; `[5,10]` and `[15,20]` can share a second one.

hints: The answer equals the largest number of meetings that are running at the same moment.
Sort by start time and keep a min-heap of end times for the rooms currently in use (or sort all starts and all ends separately and sweep with two pointers).
For each meeting, if the earliest-ending room ends at or before this start, pop it; then push this meeting's end. The maximum heap size reached is the answer.

why.d: Checks an empty `intervals` and an input whose answer is 0.

variants.title: Rooms need cleanup time
variants.approach: Min-heap of room free times · O(n log n) time
variants.statement:
Meetings are given as `[start, end)`. After a meeting ends, its room needs `buffer` extra minutes of cleaning before the next meeting can start there (a room ending at `e` is next usable at `e + buffer`).

Return the minimum number of rooms needed to hold all meetings.

examples.explanation: The second meeting starts before the first room is clean, so 2 rooms.
The room is ready exactly at 15, so 1 room suffices.

hints: Treat each meeting as occupying its room until `end + buffer`.
Keep a min-heap of the times rooms become free; reuse the earliest if it is ≤ the new start.

solutions.name: Brute Force (Peak Occupancy)
solutions.description: Treat each meeting as occupying its room over [start, end + buffer). The rooms needed equal the peak overlap, and the peak is always reached at some meeting's start, so count overlaps at every start time.
keyPoints: Peak happens at a start time

solutions.name: Min-Heap of Room Free Times (Optimal)
solutions.description: Process meetings by start time with a min-heap of the times each room becomes usable (end + buffer). If the earliest room is ready by this start, reuse it; otherwise open a new room. The heap size is the answer.

variants.title: Busiest room with delays
variants.approach: Two heaps: free rooms by index, busy rooms by end time · O(m log m + m log n)
variants.statement:
There are `n` rooms numbered `0…n-1`. Meetings `[start, end)` have **unique start times** and are handled in start order:

- A meeting takes the **lowest-numbered free room**.
- If no room is free, it waits for the room that frees up earliest (lowest number on ties) and keeps its **original duration**, starting when that room frees.

Return the room that hosted the most meetings (the lowest number on ties).

examples.explanation: Rooms end up with 2 meetings each, so room 0 wins the tie.

why.d: Checks an input whose answer is 0 and a 4 meetings.

examples.explanation: Rooms 1 and 2 each get two meetings; the answer is 1.

hints: You need the lowest free room index and the earliest-ending busy room quickly.
Use one min-heap of free room numbers and another of (end time, room) for busy rooms.
Before each meeting, release every busy room with end ≤ start; if none are free, pop the earliest busy room and push it back with end + duration.

solutions.name: Direct Simulation
solutions.description: Keep, for every room, the time it becomes free. For each meeting in start order scan rooms 0..n−1 for the first free one; if none is free, pick the room with the smallest free time (lowest index on ties) and delay the meeting to start there.

solutions.name: Two Heaps: Free Rooms by Index, Busy Rooms by End Time (Optimal)
solutions.description: A min-heap of free room numbers and a min-heap of busy rooms keyed by (end time, room). Before each meeting, release every busy room whose end ≤ start. Take the smallest free room; if none, pop the earliest-ending busy room and push it back with end + duration.

complexity.time: O(m log m + m log n)

keyPoints: No free room ⇒ delay on earliest

solutions.name: Sort + Check All Active
solutions.description: Sort by start time. Track all ongoing meetings. For each new meeting, count how many overlap.
keyPoints: For each meeting, count overlapping meetings
Maximum overlap at any point = rooms needed

solutions.name: Sweep Line (Optimal)
solutions.description: Separate start and end times, sort them, and sweep through events. Track concurrent meetings.
keyPoints: Sweep line: process starts and ends as events
Start event: +1 room, End event: -1 room
Two pointer approach on sorted start/end arrays
